negatives.failure_signature: A four-command combined inspection exceeded its ten-second execution envelope before returning output.
negatives.trigger_precondition: Several Git, Python, and large-file reads shared one short orchestration envelope.
negatives.recovery: Recorded the timeout and split inspection into bounded single-purpose commands.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Use separate commands and a measured envelope for large repository state or template reads; never infer success from a timed-out batch.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; the timed-out batch produced no validation evidence

negatives.failure_signature: The first separated retry still exceeded the same ten-second envelope while the large worktree status scan was active.
negatives.trigger_precondition: The retry separated logical checks but retained an envelope below the observed repository scan duration.
negatives.recovery: Raised only the command timeout, kept the check unchanged, and obtained exact clean branch and upstream evidence.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Use a sixty-second ceiling for large D-drive Git state checks while keeping output and query scope bounded.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; only the later completed direct checks are evidence

negatives.failure_signature: A double-quoted regular expression containing JSON quote syntax caused a PowerShell parse error before ripgrep ran.
negatives.trigger_precondition: Nested shell and regular-expression quotation was composed in one command without a literal single-quoted pattern.
negatives.recovery: Retried with a single-quoted ripgrep expression and a single target file.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Use literal single-quoted ripgrep patterns in PowerShell and avoid nested JSON quoting in composite inspection commands.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; the parse failure changed no file and supplied no evidence

negatives.operation: Method Flow explicit validation transition for V6446-M02
negatives.failure_signature: The runner rejected an explicit validated-to-validated transition because the passing witness had already advanced the method automatically.
negatives.trigger_precondition: The caller treated witness recording and validated-state promotion as separate operations without first reading the returned method state.
negatives.recovery: Retained the rejected transition and applied only the allowed validated-to-preferred transition.
negatives.recurrence_guard: After recording a witness, inspect the returned method_state; do not request validated when a passing witness has already supplied it.
negatives.promotion_effect: none for the rejected command; the separate preferred transition succeeded only after the witness had validated the method

negatives.operation: Method Flow explicit validation transition for V6446-M03
negatives.failure_signature: The runner rejected a second explicit validated-to-validated transition after the passing witness had already advanced the method.
negatives.trigger_precondition: The same batched transition assumption was repeated for the second method before the first runner error was observed.
negatives.recovery: Retained the second rejection, confirmed both methods were preferred only after successful witnesses, and preregistered a state-aware runner guard.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Run and inspect one witness result before the next state operation; use set-state preferred only from the returned validated state.
negatives.promotion_effect: none for the rejected command; no witness or negative was erased

negatives.failure_signature: The builder rejected two source additions whose URLs differed from inherited rows but whose normalized titles duplicated inherited W3C and OpenID specifications.
negatives.trigger_precondition: The preliminary slate checked canonical URLs but did not also compare normalized titles across all 200 inherited source rows.
negatives.recovery: Resolved and reused inherited source IDs V8-S09 and V6437-S147, removed both duplicate additions, and reran normalized-title and canonical-URL deduplication before the builder retry.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Compare both normalized title and canonical URL against the recursively decoded inherited ledger before assigning any new source ID.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; the rejected builder run produced no valid x1 freeze and the duplicate rows are not counted

negatives.failure_signature: The builder generated the packet but reported four expected files absent: two phase index receipts had no writer and the two validation outputs were checked before their own creation.
negatives.trigger_precondition: The inherited expected-file list outpaced its direct writer map and treated terminal self-outputs as ordinary pre-existing inputs.
negatives.recovery: Added explicit phase index writers and classified only the two terminal validation outputs as deferred self-outputs created after the presence check.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Map every expected non-self file to a writer or immutable input and keep a named minimal set of terminal self-outputs outside prewrite presence checks.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; the incomplete expected-file run is retained and only a later zero-missing build may be frozen

negatives.operation: first combined scoped x1 test run
negatives.failure_signature: The scoped run passed 55 of 56 tests; the named-validation receipt called the sequential branch authoritative but omitted the explicit canonical label required by the test and phase rule.
negatives.trigger_precondition: The receipt used a near-synonym where the frozen user boundary and validator require an exact canonical-role statement.
negatives.recovery: Changed the generated canonical_rule to name the canonical sequential branch explicitly and retained the failed 55/56 run.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Use exact frozen boundary vocabulary for canonical role, same-owner replay, and independent-reproduction limits; test the generated receipt rather than implied synonyms.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; only a later 56/56 scoped run may be promoted

negatives.operation: first exact staged-blob x1 seal review
negatives.failure_signature: All 44 staged files and 35 JSON blobs passed file-set, parse, and privacy checks, but 21 of 36 content-seal hashes differed because the seal used working-tree bytes while Git staged normalized blob bytes.
negatives.trigger_precondition: Python-generated text used Windows working-tree newlines while Git attributes and clean filters normalized the staged representation.
negatives.recovery: Changed the x1 content seal to declare and hash exact Git blob bytes produced through repository attributes and clean filters, then required staged-blob parity.
negatives.recurrence_guard: Use Git-blob SHA-256 for committed-byte manifests and keep normalized logical-text hashes as a separately named domain; never compare an undeclared working-tree domain to staged blobs.
negatives.promotion_effect: none; the 21-mismatch review is retained and only a later zero-mismatch staged review may be promoted

retention_rule: Recovery does not erase failure evidence; only successful corrected runs may be promoted.
